title: Commercial Bank Examination Manual, 3000—Capital, Earnings, Liquidity, and Sensitivity to Market Risk
summary: This Federal Reserve examination manual section explains how bank examiners assess capital adequacy under Regulation Q, detailing the three components of regulatory capital (Common Equity Tier 1, Additional Tier 1, and Tier 2) and the framework for calculating risk-weighted assets. The document is internal supervisory guidance for bank examiners, not an analysis of current macro conditions or market catalysts.
key_points: Capital adequacy triggers the most supervisory action under the Prompt Corrective Action provisions of section 38 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act (12 U.S.C. 1831o)
Regulation Q (12 CFR Part 217) was adopted in 2013 by the Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC to replace general risk-based capital, advanced approaches, market risk, and leverage capital requirements
The three components of regulatory capital are: (1) Common Equity Tier 1 capital, (2) Additional Tier 1 capital, and (3) Tier 2 capital
Common Equity Tier 1 capital is the highest-quality and most loss-absorbing form of capital, primarily composed of common stock and retained earnings
Under the standardized approach of Regulation Q, banking organizations are not required to include all components of accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI) in CET1 capital
Advanced approaches banking organizations must include most AOCI components in their Common Equity Tier 1 capital calculation
